questions.q: As we go from species to kingdom in a taxonomic hierarchy, the number of common characteristics
questions.s: Higher taxa include more diverse organisms, so the number of shared characteristics decreases as we move from species towards kingdom.

questions.q: Which of the following suffixes used for units of classification in plants indicates the taxonomic category of family?
questions.s: The names of plant families commonly end in the suffix -aceae, for example Solanaceae and Poaceae.

questions.q: The term ‘systematics’ refers to
o: identification and study of organ systems
identification and preservation of plants and animals
diversity of kinds of organisms and their relationship
study of habitats of organisms and their classification
questions.s: Systematics deals with the diversity of organisms and their relationships at every level of classification.

questions.q: Genus represents
o: a collection of plants or animals
a group of closely related species of plants or animals
questions.s: A genus comprises closely related species that share more characters with one another than with species of other genera.

questions.q: The taxonomic unit ‘Phylum’ in the classification of animals is equivalent to which hierarchical level in the classification of plants?
questions.s: Division is the corresponding taxonomic category in plants; phylum is used for animals.

questions.q: Botanical gardens and zoological parks have
o: a collection of endemic living species only
a collection of exotic living species only
a collection of endemic and exotic living species
a collection of only local plants and animals
questions.s: Botanical gardens and zoological parks maintain both endemic and exotic living species.

questions.q: A taxonomic key is one of the taxonomic tools used in the identification and classification of plants and animals. It is used in the preparation of
questions.s: Taxonomic keys help identify organisms from their characters and are used in taxonomic works such as flora and monographs.

questions.q: All living organisms are linked to one another because
o: they have common genetic material of the same type
they share common genetic material but to varying degrees
questions.s: Living organisms share genetic material, such as DNA, but its form and sequence vary among groups.

questions.q: Which of the following is a defining characteristic of living organisms?
questions.s: Response to external stimuli or to the environment is a defining property of living organisms.

questions.q:
Match Column I with Column II and choose the correct option.

Column I: A. Family; B. Kingdom; C. Order; D. Species; E. Genus
Column II: 1. Tuberosum; 2. Polymoniales; 3. Solanum; 4. Plantae; 5. Solanaceae
questions.s: The potato classification is Family—Solanaceae, Kingdom—Plantae, Order—Polymoniales, Species—tuberosum and Genus—Solanum.

questions.q: All eukaryotic unicellular organisms belong to
questions.s: Protista includes unicellular eukaryotic organisms; Monera contains prokaryotes.

questions.q: The five-kingdom classification was proposed by
questions.s: R. H. Whittaker proposed the five-kingdom classification in 1969.

questions.q: Organisms living in salty areas are called
questions.s: Halophiles are organisms adapted to habitats with high salt concentrations.

questions.q: Naked cytoplasm, multinucleate condition and saprophytic nutrition are characteristics of
questions.s: Slime moulds are saprophytic protists; their vegetative stage can be multinucleate and lacks a cell wall.

questions.q: An association between roots of higher plants and fungi is called
questions.s: Mycorrhiza is the symbiotic association between a fungus and the roots of a higher plant.

questions.q: A dikaryon is formed when
o: the two haploid cells do not fuse immediately
questions.s: After plasmogamy, the two nuclei may remain unfused for a period, producing a dikaryotic condition.

questions.q: ‘Contagium vivum fluidum’ was proposed by
questions.s: M. W. Beijerinck used the term ‘contagium vivum fluidum’ for the infectious agent now recognised as a virus.

questions.q: Association between mycobiont and phycobiont is found in
questions.s: In lichens, the fungal partner is the mycobiont and the algal partner is the phycobiont.

questions.q: The difference between a virus and a viroid is
o: absence of a protein coat in viroid, but its presence in virus
presence of low-molecular-weight RNA in virus, but its absence in viroid
questions.s: Viroids consist of RNA without a protein coat, whereas viruses possess a protein coat.

questions.q: With respect to the fungal sexual cycle, choose the correct sequence of events.
questions.s: The sequence is plasmogamy (cytoplasmic fusion), karyogamy (nuclear fusion), and then meiosis.

questions.q: Viruses are non-cellular organisms, but replicate themselves once they infect a host cell. To which kingdom do viruses belong?
questions.s: Viruses are acellular and are not placed in any of Whittaker’s five kingdoms.

questions.q:
Members of Phycomycetes are found in the following habitats or conditions:
(i) Aquatic habitats
(ii) On decaying wood
(iii) Moist and damp places
(iv) As obligate parasites on plants
Choose the correct option.
questions.s: The source’s answer key marks ‘None of these’, but its accompanying explanation states that members occur on decaying wood, in moist and damp places, and as plant parasites. The answer and explanation therefore conflict; verify against the prescribed NCERT edition before using this item for scoring.

questions.q: Cyanobacteria are classified under
questions.s: Cyanobacteria are prokaryotes and are classified under Kingdom Monera.

questions.q: Fusion of two motile gametes that are dissimilar in size is termed
questions.s: Anisogamy is the fusion of gametes that differ in size; isogamy involves similar gametes.

questions.q: Holdfast, stipe and frond constitute the plant body in
questions.s: Members of Phaeophyceae typically have a holdfast, a stipe and a leaf-like frond.

questions.q: A plant shows a thallus level of organisation, has rhizoids and is haploid. It needs water to complete its life cycle because the male gametes are motile. Identify the group.
questions.s: Bryophytes have a haploid gametophytic plant body, and their motile male gametes require water to reach the archegonium.

questions.q: A prothallus is
o: a structure in pteridophytes formed before the thallus develops
a sporophytic free-living structure formed in pteridophytes
a gametophytic free-living structure formed in pteridophytes
a primitive structure formed after fertilisation in pteridophytes
questions.s: The prothallus is the free-living gametophyte of pteridophytes, usually formed after spore germination.

questions.q: Plants of this group are diploid and well adapted to extreme conditions. They bear sporophylls in compact structures called cones. The group is
questions.s: Gymnosperms are adapted to a range of extreme conditions and bear reproductive structures in cones or strobili.

questions.q: The embryo sac of an angiosperm is made up of
questions.s: The typical mature angiosperm embryo sac is 7-celled and 8-nucleate.

questions.q: If the diploid number of a flowering plant is 36, what is the chromosome number in its endosperm?
questions.s: The endosperm is typically triploid (3n); if 2n = 36, then n = 18 and 3n = 54.

questions.q: Protonema is
o: haploid and is found in mosses
diploid and is found in liverworts
diploid and is found in pteridophytes
haploid and is found in pteridophytes
questions.s: In mosses, a haploid spore germinates to form the protonema, which develops into the gametophyte.

questions.q: The giant redwood tree (Sequoia sempervirens) is a/an
questions.s: Sequoia sempervirens is a gymnosperm.
